nextStoryContext: Fixed the reviewer-flagged doc-sync gap at docs/launch-readiness.md:31 (the 'Distribution / install: gap' section). The finding: ADR 0049 (docs/adr/0049-garboard-naming-policy-binary-alias-org-and-staged-rename.md, line 29) explicitly defers the binary rename from `cam` to `garboard`/`gar` to launch packaging, 'as a distribution item of launch readiness', and the source issue's gotchas (scripts/cam/issues/CAM-0415.json) place that same rename in the distribution dimension of this file, but the Concrete gaps list under 'Distribution / install: gap' carried no such item: the staged rename plan had no tracked home in the launch checklist it points at. Root-cause fix (single file, one new bullet appended to the existing Concrete gaps list, after the 'Install still requires a full dev toolchain' bullet and before the '## First-run onboarding' heading): added a bullet titled 'Staged product rename to `garboard`/`gar` has no tracked item here yet', citing ADR 0049's staged plan (binary moves from `cam` to `garboard`, `gar` typed alias created by the installer, `cam` demoted to an undocumented legacy symlink) and noting none of the distribution work already audited in this dimension (packaging, cross-platform builds, code signing) currently accounts for it. Deliberately left the doc's line 14 ('the display name is CAM Runtime') untouched: the reviewer finding's own remedy language ('One item in the distribution gap list closes it, mechanical, single file') scopes the fix to exactly one new gap-list item, not a rewrite of the audit header's historical framing of the prior CAM-329 rebrand state. Swept the diff for em-dash/emoji regressions post-edit (clean, zero matches). No tests reference this doc's prose, so no test changes were needed.
